research_rationale:
Executive Order 11203 (30 FR 3417, signed 1965-03-12) lets a Treasury Department employee serving under a Schedule B appointment in a position concerned with the protective function (protection of the life and safety of the President, his immediate family and others for whom similar protective services are provided by law) have the appointment converted to a career appointment on the conditions in sections 1 to 5. I read the complete held text (the text layer of the govinfo Federal Register pages, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11203.txt; identity confirmed by the order number, title, date and FR Doc. line) and confirmed the 13-clause inventory. No clause has an end in the order's own terms: the alternative 90-day period in section 1(2) that runs from the date of the order was a transition for employees already qualified in 1965, while the alternative that runs from the date the employee meets the service requirement continues, and section 4 only sets the separation date for an employee who is not recommended or fails to qualify. The only held later instrument that names this order is Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28), whose section 2-101 lists Executive Order 11203 under subsection (b) and amends each listed order by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective 1979-01-01 under section 2-404. I record that substitution as an amendment on the three clauses that named the Commission (sections 1(3), 1(4) and 5); it is not an end. Current predicate: the U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order, as amended by Executive Order 12107, in a note to 5 U.S.C. 3301 with no ending statement, and 5 U.S.C. 3301 and 7301 (the successors of the statutes the order cites, as the note brackets them) are held in force at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt and usc-t5-s7301.txt. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no revocation, supersession or ending statement; the eCFR text of 5 CFR 9701.604 (Department of Homeland Security personnel system) and the Office of Personnel Management's 2024 consolidated listing of Schedule B exceptions (89 FR 61149, FR Doc. 2024-16723) both still refer to conversion under the order, which are recitals of continued use and not changes to it. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that search; the eCFR search is stated as of 2026-10-14. The U.S. Code note and the extracted Code and eCFR texts named above are leads: their original release-point bytes are not held, so the current-law basis cited in this claim is the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches.
